subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native trust/provenance contract should OpenClaw enforce for durable memory writes and retrieval across memory-core, QMD, session memory, Memory Wiki, and plugin/MCP boundaries?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the implementation requires maintainer choices about non-forgeable trust assignment, persisted schema and migrations, public config/API shape, retrieval policy, and how much belongs in native memory versus external plugins or MCP integrations.

options.title: Design Native Trust Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the native security/product tracker and define host-authored trust metadata plus retrieval policy before implementation.

options.title: Split Provenance Foundation First
options.body: Make a durable provenance contract such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42647 canonical first, then use this issue for trust tiers, review gates, expiration, and trust-weighted retrieval.

options.title: Rely On External Integrations For Now
options.body: Treat world-model-mcp and similar integrations as optional self-serve paths while intentionally leaving native OpenClaw memory without trust enforcement.

recommendation.title: Design Native Trust Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the native security/product tracker and define host-authored trust metadata plus retrieval policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available routing signal for the memory host SDK, memory-core contract, and prior review context on this issue.
